Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith said he is awaiting "proofpoints on execution post a series of issues at the Houston manufacturing facility," primarily concerned with the impact on customer relationships and long-term market share as a result of recent missteps.
The analyst said he expected 45% Y/Y revenue growth and positive EBITDA in FY 2026 when he upgraded the stock
, but he now expects just 6% revenue growth and a $200M EBITDA loss.

"Execution risk is clearly higher than assumed, with FY26 estimates now materially lower and meaningfully less confidence in the FY27 [and beyond] fundamental story," and near-term hurdles are significant given the liquidity and history of missed expectations, Dumoulin-Smith said.
